question: Explain how Bohr’s model accounts for the line spectrum of hydrogen atom.

options.A: Bohr’s model gives a continuous spectrum because the electron can have any energy and emit any frequency.
options.B: In Bohr’s model, the electron can occupy only discrete stationary energy levels. When it falls from a higher level $E_i$ to a lower level $E_f$, it emits a photon with $h\nu=E_i-E_f$. Since only definite energy differences are possible, only definite frequencies are emitted, producing a line spectrum.
options.C: The hydrogen spectrum is continuous because stationary orbits radiate continuously.
options.D: The line spectrum is caused only by diffraction of emitted light.
